newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK 1997/98 budget unsurprising - Price Waterhouse.
newsitem.headline: HK 1997/98 budget unsurprising - Price Waterhouse.

text.p: Hong Kong's 1997/98 budget offered few surprises while stressing continuity, and its focus on personal tax allowances that benefit the middle class was welcome, accountants at Price Waterhouse said on Wednesday.

"It is consistent with all previous budgets...there has been no significant change in tax rates, tax concessions," Rod Houng-Lee, head of taxation, told Reuters. "This is very much focused on the sandwich (middle) class."

In his 1997/98 budget speech on Wednesday, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said his package of increased basic, family and training allowances and changes to tax bands would benefit 96 percent of salaried taxpayers.
Houng-Lee also welcomed Tsang's decision to increase the supply of land as a way of eventually easing pressure in the territory's booming property market.
Tsang said 327 hectares of land for public housing and 260 hectares for private housing would be released over the next five years.
That compares with land releases over the past five years of 257 hectares for public rental and subsidised ownership flats and 145 hectares for private development.
The reduction of interest withholding tax for foreign banks was also welcomed by Price Waterhouse.
"It is a good step," tax partner Tetrina Tam said.
